description: The mathematics of how robots move: rigid body motion and coordinate frames, forward and inverse kinematics of serial manipulators, velocity kinematics and the Jacobian, Lagrangian and Newton-Euler dynamics, trajectory planning and the kinematics of wheeled mobile robots. Taught with interactive browser simulations of arms and mobile robots in which every formula is implemented and tested, applied to tasks such as fruit-picking arms and warehouse or farm delivery robots.
modelledOn: Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics: Mechanics, Planning, and Control
Craig, Introduction to Robotics: Mechanics and Control
Spong, Hutchinson and Vidyasagar, Robot Modeling and Control
Siciliano, Sciavicco, Villani and Oriolo, Robotics: Modelling, Planning and Control
outcomes: Represent the position and orientation of rigid bodies with rotation matrices, Euler angles, quaternions and homogeneous transformations.
Derive the forward kinematics of serial manipulators with Denavit-Hartenberg parameters and the product of exponentials formula.
Solve inverse kinematics analytically and numerically and reason about multiple solutions, workspace and reachability.
Compute the manipulator Jacobian, identify singularities and use the Jacobian for velocity control and static force analysis.
Derive equations of motion for manipulators with Lagrangian and Newton-Euler methods and use them for simulation and computed-torque control.
Plan smooth joint-space and task-space trajectories and model, simulate and steer differential-drive and other wheeled mobile robots.

units.title: Rigid body motion and coordinate frames
topics: Robots, links, joints and degrees of freedom; Grubler's formula; configuration space and task space
Rotation matrices and the special orthogonal group; composing rotations in fixed and moving frames
Representations of orientation: Euler angles, roll-pitch-yaw, axis-angle, unit quaternions; gimbal lock
Homogeneous transformations and the special Euclidean group; chaining frames
Twists, screws and the exponential map in outline; angular velocity and skew-symmetric matrices
Visualising frames and transformations in a browser simulation

units.title: Forward kinematics
topics: Serial chains: revolute and prismatic joints, link lengths and offsets
Denavit-Hartenberg convention, standard and modified; assigning frames step by step
The product of exponentials formula as an alternative to DH parameters
Forward kinematics of planar two- and three-link arms, SCARA and a six-axis industrial arm
Workspace: reachable and dexterous workspace; plotting it by sampling joint space

units.title: Inverse kinematics
topics: The inverse problem: existence, multiple solutions, elbow-up and elbow-down configurations
Analytical solutions for planar arms and the spherical wrist by kinematic decoupling
Numerical inverse kinematics: Newton-Raphson, Jacobian transpose and damped least squares
Joint limits, redundancy and choosing among solutions
Inverse kinematics for a fruit-picking or sorting arm reaching targets detected by a camera

units.title: Velocity kinematics and the Jacobian
topics: Linear and angular velocity of the end effector; the geometric and analytical Jacobian
Computing the Jacobian column by column; the space and body Jacobians
Singularities: boundary and interior singularities, loss of mobility, manipulability ellipsoids
Resolved-rate motion control and the pseudo-inverse for redundant arms
Statics: the Jacobian transpose relating end-effector forces to joint torques

units.title: Dynamics of manipulators
topics: Mass properties: centre of mass, inertia tensors, the parallel axis theorem
Lagrangian dynamics: kinetic and potential energy, the Euler-Lagrange equations for a two-link arm
Recursive Newton-Euler formulation and its computational efficiency
The manipulator equation: mass matrix, Coriolis and centrifugal terms, gravity; properties used in control
Forward dynamics for simulation; numerical integration and its stability
Joint-space control: PD with gravity compensation and computed-torque control; actuator and friction models

units.title: Trajectory planning
topics: Paths versus trajectories; time scaling
Point-to-point motion with cubic and quintic polynomials; trapezoidal velocity profiles
Via points and spline interpolation; blending segments
Task-space straight-line and circular paths; interpolating orientations with quaternion slerp
Time-optimal trajectories under velocity, acceleration and torque limits in outline

units.title: Kinematics of mobile robots
topics: Wheel types and constraints; holonomic and non-holonomic systems
Differential-drive kinematics: instantaneous centre of rotation, forward and inverse kinematics
Car-like, tricycle and omnidirectional (mecanum) platforms
Odometry from wheel encoders, error growth and dead reckoning
Path following: pure pursuit and simple feedback controllers for go-to-goal behaviour
Mobile robots in African settings: farm robots between crop rows and delivery robots on campus paths
Project: a simulated arm or mobile robot that completes a pick-and-place or delivery task

schedule.title: Degrees of freedom and rotations
schedule.exercise: Problem set: compute the degrees of freedom of four mechanisms with Grubler's formula and compose three rotation matrices by hand.

tasks.title: Count the degrees of freedom of a planar four-bar linkage and a six-axis arm using Grubler's formula and check each result
Compose a rotation of 30 degrees about Z and 45 about X in fixed and then moving frames, and show the results differ
Convert one orientation between roll-pitch-yaw, axis-angle and quaternion, and show a gimbal lock case where two Euler angles collapse

schedule.title: Homogeneous transforms and frames
schedule.exercise: Chain three coordinate frames on paper and find the position of a gripper point in the base frame.

tasks.title: Build a 4x4 homogeneous transform from a rotation and translation and use it to map three points between frames
Compute the skew-symmetric matrix of an angular velocity, form the rotation with the exponential map and check it is orthogonal
Visualise a chain of three frames in the browser, apply transform sequences and verify the end frame against your hand calculation

schedule.title: DH parameters and exponentials
schedule.exercise: Assign DH frames to a three-link arm on a sketch, write the parameter table and compare with the product of exponentials form.

tasks.title: Fill in the DH table for a planar two-link arm and write the two transform matrices for given joint angles
Assign frames and the DH table for a three-joint arm with an offset, then multiply the matrices to get the end-effector pose
Compute forward kinematics of a 3R arm with the product of exponentials and check it agrees with the DH result to six decimals

schedule.title: Forward kinematics and workspace
schedule.exercise: Compute the end-effector position of a SCARA and a six-axis arm for given joint values and sketch their workspaces.

tasks.title: Compute and plot the end-effector position of a planar two-link arm for joint angles of 0, 45 and 90 degrees
Program forward kinematics for a SCARA robot and a six-axis arm and check the pose against hand calculations for three configurations
Sample the joint space of a three-link planar arm to plot its reachable workspace and identify its dexterous region and holes

schedule.title: Inverse kinematics
schedule.exercise: Solve inverse kinematics of a two-link arm analytically for a target, identifying both elbow solutions.

tasks.title: Solve a planar two-link arm for a target at (1.2, 0.8) analytically and verify both elbow-up and elbow-down solutions with forward kinematics
Solve inverse kinematics for a three-link arm with Newton-Raphson and with damped least squares and compare iterations to converge
Find all inverse kinematics solutions of a spherical-wrist arm by decoupling position and orientation, and test unreachable and singular targets

schedule.title: Redundancy and the picking arm
schedule.exercise: Describe how a fruit-picking arm should choose among solutions with joint limits and obstacles in the way.

tasks.title: Choose among several inverse kinematics solutions of a two-link arm by joint limits and minimum joint motion from the current pose
Reach ten camera-detected targets with a planar arm, handle unreachable ones and report the position error at each
Resolve the redundancy of a four-link planar arm by minimising joint motion while avoiding a joint limit and compare two secondary objectives

schedule.title: The Jacobian and singularities
schedule.exercise: Derive the Jacobian of a two-link arm by hand and find its singular configurations.

tasks.title: Compute the 2x2 Jacobian of a planar two-link arm at three configurations and map a joint velocity to end-effector velocity
Compute the Jacobian of a three-link arm column by column and check it against a numerical derivative of forward kinematics
Plot the manipulability ellipse of a two-link arm across its workspace and find the configurations where the determinant is zero

schedule.title: Resolved-rate control and statics
schedule.exercise: Compute the joint torques needed to hold a 2 kg load with a two-link arm using the Jacobian transpose.

tasks.title: Compute joint torques needed to apply a 10 N force at the end effector of a two-link arm in a given pose
Move a three-link arm's end effector along a line using resolved-rate control with the pseudo-inverse and plot the tracking error
Compare the pseudo-inverse and damped least squares controllers while the arm passes near a singularity and report the joint velocities

schedule.title: Mass properties and Lagrangian dynamics
schedule.exercise: Derive the equations of motion for a two-link arm by the Euler-Lagrange method and compare with the standard form.

tasks.title: Compute the centre of mass and inertia tensor of a composite link with the parallel axis theorem for a uniform rod and a box
Derive the kinetic and potential energy of a two-link arm and obtain its equations of motion with the Euler-Lagrange equations
Implement recursive Newton-Euler for a three-link arm, verify it against the Lagrangian result and compare the operation counts

schedule.title: Manipulator equation and joint control
schedule.exercise: Tune a PD controller with gravity compensation for a two-link arm and explain what computed-torque control adds.

tasks.title: Compute the mass matrix, Coriolis and gravity terms of a two-link arm at a given state and verify the symmetry of the mass matrix
Simulate the free fall of a two-link arm under gravity with two integrators and compare energy drift at 1 ms and 10 ms steps
Compare PD with gravity compensation and computed-torque control on a two-link arm following a step command with friction and report the error

schedule.title: Trajectory planning
schedule.exercise: Plan a three-point trajectory for a pick-and-place task and check velocity and acceleration against joint limits.

tasks.title: Fit a cubic polynomial between two joint positions with zero end velocities and plot the position, velocity and acceleration
Interpolate three via points with a cubic spline and find where the acceleration exceeds a joint limit
Plan a straight-line task-space move with quaternion slerp for the orientation and check the joint trajectory stays within limits

schedule.title: Mobile robot kinematics
schedule.exercise: Derive the differential-drive kinematics equations and calculate the radius of curvature for given wheel speeds.

tasks.title: Compute the velocity and turning radius of a differential-drive robot from left and right wheel speeds and simulate a 10-second path
Simulate wheel-encoder odometry with small noise and plot how position error grows over a 50-metre square path
Compare the kinematic models of a car-like and a mecanum platform and find which can move sideways, then plan a parking manoeuvre for one

schedule.title: Path following and the pick-and-place project
schedule.exercise: Project plan: specify the task, robot model, controller and test cases for a simulated farm or delivery robot.

tasks.title: Implement pure pursuit for a differential-drive robot along a waypoint path and plot the tracking error
Make a farm robot drive between crop rows and turn at the end of each row with a go-to-goal controller and report the row-end overshoot
Complete a simulated pick-and-place or campus delivery task with kinematics, a controller and a trajectory, and report success over 20 randomised runs
